title: Partial, Required, Pick, and Omit
hook: Partial<T> makes every property optional for update DTOs; Required<T> does the opposite. Pick<T, K> and Omit<T, K> slice object shapes without duplicating field definitions — the bread and butter of API layer typing.

blocks.text: **Partial<T>** maps every key in `T` to optional: `{ [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }`. **Required<T>** removes optionality from all keys. **Pick<T, K>** keeps only keys `K` from `T`: `{ [P in K]: T[P] }` where `K extends keyof T`. **Omit<T, K>** excludes keys: `Pick<T, Exclude<keyof T, K>>`. All are **mapped types** — compile-time transforms that produce new object types. They erase completely — no runtime objects created.

entries.plainDefinition: All properties of T become optional.
All properties of T become required.
Subset of T with only keys K.

blocks.text: REST PATCH endpoints accept `Partial<User>`. Form submission uses `Pick<User, 'email' | 'password'>`. Public API responses use `Omit<User, 'internalId' | 'ssn'>`. Without utilities, teams copy-paste interfaces and drift from the source of truth. C# has no built-in Partial — uses records with `with` or manual DTOs. Senior interviews ask you to **implement** Pick/Omit from scratch using mapped types and keyof.

blocks.title: Single source of truth
blocks.body: Define full Entity once — derive CreateDto, UpdateDto, PublicView with Pick/Omit/Partial.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

snippet.label: PATCH with Partial
snippet.explanation: Line 8: Partial makes all fields optional except id is omitted entirely. Line 13: partial update type-safe.

snippet.label: Pick and Omit for views
snippet.explanation: Line 1: public profile fields only. Line 4: create body without id. Line 6: compose utilities — email required, rest optional.

snippet.label: Implementing Pick from scratch
snippet.explanation: Lines 1-3: mapped type iterates K keys. Line 5: Omit via Exclude on keyof. Same as built-in utilities.

snippet.label: Failure mode — Partial on nested objects
snippet.explanation: Partial is shallow — optional top-level keys only. Nested objects need DeepPartial custom type.

blocks.title: Shallow Partial on nested
blocks.body: Partial<Profile> does not make Profile.user.email optional — need DeepPartial.

blocks.title: Pick with invalid key
blocks.body: Pick<User, 'foo'> errors — K must extend keyof T.

blocks.text: Combine with `&` intersection: `Partial<User> & { id: string }` for id-required partial. `Omit<User, keyof AdminOnly>` using helper types. Readonly variants: `Readonly<Pick<T, K>>`. Performance: mapped types are compile-time only — zero bundle impact. Large unions can slow tsserver — split entities. `satisfies` validates derived object literals against Pick/Omit shapes.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot implement Pick from mapped types. Thinks Partial is deep. Pick/Omit keys not constrained to keyof T.

interviewTakeaways: Partial = all optional; Required = all required; Pick = subset keys; Omit = exclude keys.
All are mapped types over keyof T — compile-time only.
Derive Create/Update/Public DTOs from one Entity.
60s: Partial for PATCH. Pick/Omit slice shapes. Implement with [K in keyof T]. Shallow only — DeepPartial for nested. Foundation of API typing.
Follow-up: compose with Record, Exclude, DeepPartial implementation.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "Partial makes nested fields optional" — shallow only.
Duplicating DTO interfaces instead of Pick/Omit.
Strong: "Mapped types over keyof. Pick [P in K]: T[P]. Omit via Exclude. Derive DTOs from canonical Entity."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS object spread copies runtime fields — TS Pick/Omit describe compile-time shape without runtime transformation.
C# record with expressions copy at runtime; TS Pick/Omit are type-level only — no emitted code.
